newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell says committed to sustainable development.
newsitem.headline: Shell says committed to sustainable development.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group's chairman said on Monday the company was committed to sustainable development, but environmental groups are yet to be convinced.
Cor Herkstroeter said Shell wished to address the problems of localised and global environmental damage and the finite nature of resources.

"Shell companies will commit themselves to pursuing the goals of causing no harm to people and to protecting the environment...As with our business principles, new procedures are being adopted to help ensure that our deeds match our aspirations," he told an audience of business students at Erasmus University in Rotterdam.
He added that Shell realised energy emissions risked changing the global climate, making action essential.
"Despite the many remaining uncertainties about the nature and risks of this process, I believe that there is now sufficient evidence to support prudent precautionary action," he said.

Herkstroeter said Shell would encourage energy-saving measures and the use of renewables and would also support a European directive limiting air pollutants in line with the conclusions of the Auto-Oil project.
Shell would shortly publish a paper outlining the company's thoughts on the subject.
Environmental group Milieu Defensie, incorporated with Friends of the Earth, said it was sceptical about Shell's environmental claims.
"Milieu Defensie is sceptical...so long as the company does not agree to independent tests of its environmental activities," Milieu Defensie said in a statement.
Milieu Defensie was particularly keen to see Shell's activities in Nigeria scrutinised, said campaigner Irene Bloemink.

"We have had talks (with Shell) to compose a group of independent experts seen as neutral to look at Shell in Nigeria. They have said in general they are pro-environment, but they are not willing to release information," Bloemink said.
No-one at Shell was immediately available for comment.
